message.content:
**How to kill Visual Studio Code (code.exe) from the command line** | What you want to do | Command | Notes | |---------------------|---------|-------| | **Kill *all* running `code.exe` processes immediately** | ```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F
``` | `/IM` specifies the image name (`code.exe`).
`/F` forces termination (no prompt). | | **Kill a *specific* instance by its Process ID (PID)** | ```cmd
taskkill /PID /F
``` | Replace `` with the number shown in Task Manager or `tasklist`. | | **Kill *and* all child processes** | ```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
``` | `/T` terminates the specified process and any child processes started by it. | | **Use a filter (e.g., only kill if the window title contains “VS Code”)** | ```cmd
taskkill /FI "WINDOWTITLE eq *VS Code*" /F
``` | Filters based on window title; useful when multiple apps share the same executable name. | ### Quick‑start: Kill everything at once 1. Open **Command Prompt** (or PowerShell) as Administrator. 2. Run: ```cmd taskkill /IM code.exe /F ``` This will close all VS Code windows instantly—any unsaved changes will be lost, so make sure you’re ready to lose data. ### If you need to target a particular instance 1. Find the PID(s): ```cmd tasklist | findstr code.exe ``` Example output: ``` code.exe 1234 Console 1 45,678 K code.exe 5678 Console 1 12,345 K ``` 2. Kill the desired one: ```cmd taskkill /PID 1234 /F ``` ### Using PowerShell (alternative) If you prefer PowerShell, you can stop the process like this: ```powershell Stop-Process -Name code -Force ``` Or by PID: ```powershell Stop-Process -Id 1234 -Force ``` --- #### ⚠️ Caution - **Unsaved Work:** All of these methods force the application to quit without prompting to save. Make sure you’ve saved your files beforehand. - **Administrator Rights:** Some instances may require elevated privileges to terminate. If you see “Access denied,” try running the console as Administrator. That’s it! Use whichever variant fits your situation.
